clue.text: God is filling a noted hole — thinking to the contrary?

indicators.note: filling means the pair of words for God is goes inside the cash machine

parts.note: a hole in the wall dispensing banknotes is a cash machine, an ATM
God is referred to as He

explanation.surface: Someone muses on God plugging a famous gap, wondering if the opposite is true.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hole in the wall' is British slang for a cash machine, and it is 'noted' because it dispenses banknotes; God is conventionally called He.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbelief in any deity is thinking contrary to faith in God, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Possible hand or paw, it could be?

indicators.note: could be invites the letters of these words to become something else

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a paw might count as a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker, two pairs of matching cards make one of the ranked hands.
explanation.definitionFit: This combination of cards is one of the recognised poker holdings, so a possible hand.

clue.text: Top card game, toss of a coin?

indicators.note: Top means the first letter is cut off the card game

parts.note: sevens is a card game where sevens are laid out first

explanation.surface: A card game is billed as the best, as random as a coin toss.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin toss has equal odds either way, which bookmakers call even money.

clue.text: Loosely scatter half of this oath

parts.note: to strew is to scatter things loosely about

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of this

explanation.surface: An instruction to toss about half of some oath.
explanation.walkthrough: Strewth is an old British and Australian exclamation, a contraction of 'God's truth'.
explanation.definitionFit: This mild exclamation of surprise is a form of swearing, a minced oath.

clue.text: A date of despair for Poland, cold — and clean

parts.note: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, written SEPT I
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A grim anniversary in Polish history is recalled, chilly yet somehow clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Something free of germs and contamination is sterile, which is to say clean.

clue.text: 17 behind the times?

definitions.meaning: 17 is the answer to the clue Form of fish, a perch: a geometric figure of four equal sides is one such form

explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided figure is a form, and an unfashionable person is called this as slang.

clue.text: Swinging crawler, not entirely supportive of Paul, regularly pinching bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue the crawler piece sits below, so it supports the part from Paul
pinching means the alternate letters of Paul close round the word for bottom
regularly takes every other letter of Paul, the first and third

parts.note: the bottom of something is its end

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the insect is dropped

parts.note: a louse is a crawling insect

explanation.surface: The setter Paul mocks a sycophant hanging around him, while a backside gets nipped.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is the setter's own pseudonym, so the surface is a self-portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pendulous hangs down loosely and sways, so it is swinging.

clue.text: Second engineer isn't against taking foot off

indicators.note: engineer is a verb here, meaning to rearrange the letters of the word isn't
the foot of a down entry is its last letter, which is removed

parts.note: anti means against

explanation.surface: An engineer who is not opposed gets his foot removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment or very short time, as in wait a second, is a synonym.

clue.text: Catholic among 19 converts in total forgetting biblical text relating to 1712

indicators.note: among means the Catholic abbreviation sits inside the rearranged letters
converts means the letters of nineteen and the trimmed total are changed into something new

parts.note: the number written out in words

indicators.note: forgetting means the letters for biblical text are dropped from total

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament
RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A Catholic among nineteen converts is tallied without scripture, regarding some year.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' here is the number spelt out, not a cross-reference. The puzzle appeared in 2012, three hundred years after 1712.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-hundredth anniversary celebration in 2012 would mark events of the year 1712.

clue.text: One part of a shoe

definitions.meaning: only, single, as in the one survivor

explanation.definitionFit: Sole means only one, and it is also the bottom surface of footwear.

clue.text: Spreading of flu ensures sorry feeling

indicators.note: spreading means the letters of flu ensures are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: An outbreak of influenza guarantees people feel miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rueful is regretful or sorrowful, so this noun is a sorry feeling.

clue.text: European city's action, which may be 13

parts.note: military action is war
13 is the answer to O such a letter?: a saw with a round blade is that kind

explanation.surface: A city's events are described as action, with a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital of Poland, a European city.

clue.text: O such a letter?

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape, and a letter sent to many people is a mailshot of that name

explanation.definitionFit: An O is round in shape, and a mass-mailed notice is called this, so both readings fit.

clue.text: Bear round object that may be 13

indicators.note: round means the letters of bear are turned about into a new order

parts.note: an object is a thing

explanation.surface: A bear rounds on some object.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to 13 across: wind players use a circular technique to sustain a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Circular respiration is a recognised technique of continuous inhaling and exhaling for wind players.

clue.text: Desire topless lust after squeezing softly favourite uncle's rear

indicators.note: squeezing means the trimmed word for lust after closes round the next pieces
topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to fancy someone is to lust after them
P is piano, the musical direction for softly
a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: rear means the last letter of uncle

explanation.surface: Craving, a topless figure is lusted after while hugging a favourite uncle softly.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetency is a formal word for a longing or craving, a desire.

clue.text: Penny spent training here, not the full shilling

definitions.meaning: a child learning toilet habits spends a penny, British slang for urinating, in this small pot
British idiom for mentally lacking, a shilling being an old coin

explanation.definitionFit: A child's chamber pot is used in toilet training, and as slang the word means crazy.

clue.text: Form of fish, a perch

indicators.note: of means the answer is made of letters running across fish, a perch

explanation.surface: A fisherman describes the build of a perch.
explanation.definitionFit: Form and outline are synonyms for the contour of something.

clue.text: Man on board's call for dismissal

definitions.meaning: a sailor's cry when hauling ropes together
to give someone the push is to dismiss them

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors chanted this while hauling; getting the same phrase as slang means being sacked.

clue.text: Not as much to say, as one 6?

indicators.note: to say signals that the word for not as much is spoken, and sounds like the answer

parts.note: lesser means smaller in amount, not as much

explanation.surface: Someone has less to say, being a square.
explanation.walkthrough: The city name is pronounced roughly 'Lester'. Leicester Square is a well-known square in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The London landmark pairs the city name with the word for a four-sided plaza, so it is one such place.

clue.text: Baldie holding nerve somersaulting, as assistant in the air

indicators.note: holding means the bird contains the turned word for nerve

parts.note: the coot has a white bald patch, hence bald as a coot

indicators.note: somersaulting turns the word for nerve head over heels, backwards

parts.note: lip is cheek, impudence or nerve

explanation.surface: A bald man keeps his nerve while doing aerobatics as a flight assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: The second pilot of an aircraft assists the captain, so an assistant in the air.

clue.text: Summon from the grave the oldest woman to possess old Tom

indicators.note: to possess means the first woman's name holds the other pieces

parts.note: Eve, the first woman in Genesis
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: The world's oldest woman owns a geriatric tomcat, and is called back from death.
explanation.definitionFit: To evocate is to call up spirits, conjuring the dead back to the living.

clue.text: Island off Cornwall runs into what's destroying the high street?

indicators.note: into means the cricket abbreviation goes inside the supermarket name

parts.note: Tesco, the British supermarket giant blamed for killing small town-centre shops
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A complaint that a supermarket chain is wrecking traditional shopping streets.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesco is Britain's largest supermarket chain; the high street is a British town's main shopping street.
explanation.definitionFit: Tresco is one of the Isles of Scilly, which lie off the Cornish coast.

clue.text: Certain disgraceful riots captured on film?

indicators.note: captured on means the rearranged letters are held inside the film container

parts.note: a can holds a reel of film, hence in the can

indicators.note: disgraceful suggests the riot letters are in a shameful mess

explanation.surface: Shameful rioting is definitely recorded on camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast-iron guarantee is unbreakable, so the adjective means certain.

clue.text: See 27
Tracker from the north or south?

indicators.note: in a down entry reading from top or bottom gives the same letters

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A tracking device that works whichever way it faces.
explanation.definitionFit: This system detects and follows aircraft and ships, a tracking device.

clue.text: Bouncer's son fettered by bit of a writer wearing a tie

indicators.note: wearing means the score round the pen point, as if dressed in it

parts.note: a ten-all score is a tie

indicators.note: fettered by means the son abbreviation is held inside the pen point

parts.note: a nib is part of a pen

explanation.surface: A nightclub bouncer's son is shackled to a writer in a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball used at Wimbledon is made to bounce, so it is a bouncer.

clue.text: Sketch of 28, say?

parts.note: 28 is a figure with many sides, which said aloud is Polly gone: a pet bird expired, the subject of a Monty Python sketch

explanation.definitionFit: The famous Monty Python routine features a dead Norwegian Blue, and a bird named Polly gone is that.

clue.text: 17 unknown, cut back, almost disappeared

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read in reverse

parts.note: to lop is to cut
Y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: gone means disappeared

explanation.surface: A form of unknown was trimmed away until nearly vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: A many-sided plane figure is a geometric form, the shape at 17.

clue.text: Young player getting old, clutching right thigh at kick-off?

indicators.note: clutching means the word for old holds the abbreviation for right

parts.note: stale means old

indicators.note: at kick-off means the opening letter of thigh

explanation.surface: A young footballer ageing clutches a hamstring as the match begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A starlet is a young actress or promising young sportsperson, a young player.
